title: fix(update): explain target metadata preflight failures
body:
Related: #151589. Thanks to @Nsikak1 for the bounded update failure report.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an update refusal that reports only `target-metadata-preflight` and `mode: unknown`, leaving the operator without a useful cause or next step.

## User Impact

Updates preserve the detected npm, pnpm, Bun, or Git mode and explain which target metadata could not be inspected. Unclassifiable installations skip before target lookup with the inspected root, Git metadata, node_modules layout, service target, and recovery commands. Unowned installs remain successful skips with no package replacement or Gateway restart.

The new diagnostics appear in terminal summaries, JSON results and recorded `update status --json` history. Bounded public reports retain fixed descriptions and next steps without exposing local paths or raw registry responses. No options, dependencies, or database schemas change. This repairs the candidate's updater; an installed updater that refuses before staging cannot pick up the fix, and old reports cannot establish which unrecorded metadata check failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported unknown mode was not proof of failed installation detection: the terminal reporting boundary discarded every known non-Git mode. Installation inspection also treated every non-Git directory as a package, including missing or invalid manifests. The fix validates package identity at inspection, carries the resolved manager into terminal outcomes, and uses existing failure-fact and ledger fields for typed metadata diagnostics. Fresh-target admission stays with the target owner, and public reporting projects approved fixed messages from those codes. Skip diagnostics enrich the existing admission phase so `update repair` still acknowledges an untouched installation without finalization.

## Evidence

Compatibility proof for source head `d2bd9233a302a49b6f19996e393bccc5936cfdb3`, compared with pinned main `308113ca06bb4c2d2a8fa5e9c0c075d3f293d1c2` (includes Homebrew #141011). Per the maintainer's ruling, this exercises the changed classifier as the **candidate driver × real install shapes**. The published 2026.9.4 driver does not execute this new classifier.

[Linux Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35343144649): Linux/x64, Node 24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, global pnpm 12.4.2, Bun 1.4.2. Both drivers ran all eight shapes below. Each package fixture started with a real published `openclaw@2026.9.4` install through its package manager. Every cell used an isolated HOME, state/config paths, empty npm configs, and a free loopback port.

| Install shape | Update/preview mode | Main outcome | Candidate outcome | Preflight and shown recovery guidance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm global, default prefix | `npm` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| npm global, custom `npm_config_prefix` | `npm` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| pnpm global | `pnpm` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| Bun global | `bun` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| npm root through a symlink | `npm` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| npm prefix containing spaces | `npm` | Updated, exit 0 | Updated, exit 0 | Passed; Doctor/cleanup guidance below |
| Real Git checkout | `git` | Dry-run exit 0 | Dry-run exit 0 | Target preview passed; no metadata-failure recovery command |
| Homebrew Cellar layout and opt alias | `unknown` (existing wire enum) | Typed skip, exit 0 | Same typed skip, exit 0 | `unmanaged-package-install`; `brew upgrade openclaw-cli`, then `openclaw gateway restart` |

All **12 actual package updates** completed staging and activation, verified the installed target's build-info against the candidate artifact, and recorded `lastRun.status: "succeeded"` in `openclaw update status --json`, with no failure facts. Both drivers printed the same non-blocking loopback Doctor advisory and `openclaw doctor --fix`, plus `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` after verifying history. Those warnings did not turn successful updates into failures.

Homebrew is positively recognized by its owner: both Cellar and opt paths return `status: "skipped"`, `reason: "unmanaged-package-install"`, `steps: []`, and the brew/restart guidance. Neither emits `installation-unclassified`. The existing status inspection reports the package/npm layout; the actual update owner emits the Homebrew skip. This preserves main's outcome without adding an enum or schema. Git status records `installKind: "git"`; its updater preview records `mode: "git"`.

Sanitized final proof output:

```text
MATRIX_RUN_EXITS main=0 candidate=0
MATRIX_COMPARISON={"problems":[]}
blacksmith run summary: command=20m12.757s, exit=0
Testbox stopped (completed)
```

<details>
<summary>Commands and artifact provenance</summary>

Canonical builds used repository pnpm 12.4.0:

```sh
node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs \
  --output-dir "$OUT" --output-name candidate.tgz --allow-unreleased-changelog
```

Real published install setup (separate isolated environments; the first command uses the Testbox Node toolchain's default global prefix):

```sh
npm install --global openclaw@2026.9.4 --allow-scripts=openclaw
npm_config_prefix="$PREFIX" npm install --global openclaw@2026.9.4 --allow-scripts=openclaw
PNPM_HOME="$P" PATH="$P/bin:$P:$PATH" \
  pnpm add --global --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@2026.9.4
BUN_INSTALL="$P" bun add --global --trust openclaw@2026.9.4
```

Read-only inspection first loaded each selected built driver through a temporary launcher in the published root and verified that the CLI selected that actual installed root. The launcher and its empty directory were removed before mutation. Then the same real package manager installed the selected driver artifact into that shape:

```sh
npm install --global "$DRIVER_TGZ" "--allow-scripts=$DRIVER_TGZ"
pnpm add --global --allow-build=openclaw "$DRIVER_TGZ"
bun add --global --trust "openclaw@file:$DRIVER_TGZ"
```

After verifying the installed driver's build-info, the normal installed CLI performed the tarball-targeted update and durable-history check:

```sh
node "$INSTALLED_ROOT/openclaw.mjs" update \
  --tag "$CANDIDATE_TGZ" --yes --json --no-restart
node "$INSTALLED_ROOT/openclaw.mjs" update status --json
```

Git used a real clone with status and dry-run, without a tarball tag. Homebrew used `<prefix>/Cellar/openclaw-cli/2026.9.4/libexec/lib/node_modules/openclaw` and the `<prefix>/opt/openclaw-cli` symlink with `HOMEBREW_PREFIX=<prefix>`, checking status and dry-run through both paths.

- Candidate/target tarball SHA-256: `2f278937f7c99a285f63bf3d2679f03a93826d2aa1d8c1f513e09a771ee645c7`.
- Main control tarball SHA-256: `002494f673200e730ce71b132a4d2b680c43392dcb2d359d5adbbd15d3ecf402`.
- Candidate source tree: `49c4fdc952ef44c83ab421a4c55ff78b97b04d7a`. The build wrapper verified source head `d2bd9233a302a49b6f19996e393bccc5936cfdb3` against that tree and generated build carrier `886c5da61100179301bfed5f8c0e474be193ef08`; the carrier commit, rather than the source-head SHA, appears in build-info.
- Candidate build-info SHA-256: `350f2ba36d87f767504dd4b58280251a8d5238702bd91116a2f0b4c0851637d3`. Every installed target matched it.

Both canonical builds and package integrity checks passed. Final complete matrix records and both verified tarballs were retained locally before Testbox cleanup. Earlier disposable harness attempts are excluded from the passing matrix; no product safety check or timeout was weakened. All task Testboxes are stopped. The linked Actions lease can show cancelled after deliberate cleanup; the successful wrapper exit and recorded matrix are the proof result.

</details>

**Owner correction and review:** The old head lacked main's Homebrew ownership path and previewed an npm update for a Cellar install. Rebase retained main's Homebrew resolver before generic manager detection. The correction supplies an explicit empty failure-facts array for Homebrew's intentional skip, preserving the existing `steps: []` and guidance. A stale generic-diagnostic assertion now checks the typed unclassifiable outcome and actual error class; the Homebrew flow assertions were unchanged.

Fresh Linux proof passed **50 tests** across installation classification, Homebrew handling, CLI layouts, command-runner errors, and metadata diagnostics:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-install-layout.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-homebrew.test.ts \
  src/infra/update-check-install-kind.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/update-command-metadata-diagnostics.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs
```

`check:changed` passed in full on Linux. Fresh Codex committed-branch autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1`, private Darwin `TMPDIR`) was **scoped-clean** on `d2bd9233a302a49b6f19996e393bccc5936cfdb3`. Production: +266/-47; tests/support: +473/-44; docs: +9/-0 versus the pinned main. No suppression or baseline changes.

**Exact-head CI:** `node scripts/watch-pr-ci.mjs 151649 6f179ca22d19a398c6172443077e5f2e886b95c8` returned **GREEN**, exit 0, with `rollup=green github_rollup=SUCCESS pending=0 superseded=0` on [run 35355091194](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35355091194). The earlier conflict verdict is superseded. No CI rerun was requested.

**Latest review:** [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151649#issuecomment-5728039277) at 2026-09-18 14:26 UTC covers exact head `6f179ca22d19a398c6172443077e5f2e886b95c8`: no correctness/security findings and no Before merge or Rank-up actions remain. It verified that all 19 changed production files match the compatibility-proof head byte-for-byte. The committed-branch Codex review is scoped-clean; intervening conflict resolutions preserve package-mode reporting, both lifecycle test setups, and Homebrew's typed skip.

**Earlier diagnostic proof retained:** Twelve original failure regressions failed against the original production code for the intended missing diagnostics; the valid-artifact control passed. Prior focused proof covered 297 tests. Isolated checks showed an empty root producing `installation-unclassified` with inspection evidence and recovery commands, and the registered CLI using real npm against inconsistent loopback-registry metadata produced `mode: npm`, `target-version-resolution`, and a retry command. The dry-run left its isolated state directory empty. This proves clearer diagnostics, not recovery of the reporter's still-unidentified underlying failure.



Selected fields from the isolated macOS / Node 26.8.2 proof output:

```json
{
  "unclassifiableRoot": {
    "installKind": "unknown",
    "code": "installation-unclassified",
    "message": "Installation ownership could not be determined. Run openclaw gateway status --deep and npm root -g; retry openclaw update from the owning installation or reinstall using the original method."
  },
  "brokenMetadata": {
    "status": "error",
    "mode": "npm",
    "reason": "target-metadata-preflight",
    "failureFact": {
      "check": "target-metadata-preflight",
      "code": "target-version-resolution",
      "message": "The target version is missing, invalid, or differs from the requested release. Verify the published version, then retry openclaw update --tag <published-version>."
    }
  }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Original-owner inventory and scope</summary>

Locations below refer to baseline `90f47f2e7a0076308f387a33e1faec85a11408ac`, before lines shifted.

| Unknown classification or mode | Original source |
| --- | --- |
| Null root gives unknown install kind; every other non-Git root was assumed to be a package | `src/infra/update-check.ts:225,238,655` |
| Package manager could not be detected | `src/infra/update-check.ts:216,680` |
| Missing/unknown install surface, or package with no global owner | `src/infra/update-runner-install-surface.ts:107,122` |
| No OpenClaw package root, or Git root without an OpenClaw package | `src/infra/update-runner.ts:57,78` |
| Package-to-CLI skip discarded a known global manager | `src/infra/update-runner.ts:95` |
| Every non-Git pre-mutation outcome discarded its detected mode | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-terminal.ts:359` |

Other `unknown` modes are fallback envelopes, not installation decisions: pending package recovery (`update-command-run.ts:156`), unsupported Node (`:497`), activation timeout (`update-command-terminal.ts:93`), admission/busy/ownership errors (`update-command-result.ts:138,180`), missing triage result (`update-command-report.ts:68`), generic unwind (`update-command-unwind.ts:31`), finalization timeout (`update-finalization-lifecycle.ts:317`), post-plugin failure (`update-command-finalize.ts:467`), resume output (`update-command-resume.ts:176`), and managed handoff sentinel (`src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts:522`). CLI paths in this paragraph are under `src/cli/update-cli/`.

Every direct metadata-preflight producer:

| Failure | Original source |
| --- | --- |
| Exact registry lookup error or missing/mismatched returned version | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-target.ts:370` |
| Fresh profile lacks resolved version or schema support | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:247` |
| Artifact version is invalid or schema declaration missing/invalid | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-artifact.ts:103,147` |
| Git target metadata unreadable | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-git-admission.ts:29,48` |
| Git dry-run metadata unreadable | `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-schema.ts:175` |
| New Git checkout has no inspected target | `src/infra/update-runner-git.ts:474` |

Git metadata inspection fails on thrown/nonzero `git show` or invalid JSON (`update-runner-git-target.ts:213,216,231`). Preview additionally reports unavailable/ambiguous remotes or revisions, missing local objects/tags, conflicting remote tag SHAs, unsupported Git channel, or a symbolic target requiring fetch (`update-command-git.ts:184,216,230,243,302,312,317,326,343,359,396`). Unresolved npm dist-tag/version lookups previously lost specificity at `update-command-target.ts:329` and `shared.ts:188`.

Tarball integrity is not a target-metadata check: it belongs to package staging (`package-update-steps.ts:606`, `update-command-package.ts:403`) and already carries `EINTEGRITY`. Channel-policy and destination-ownership refusals also have distinct existing owners/reasons. This patch does not invent new integrity, channel, or install-root gates.

</details>
